newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude may bounce but still bearish.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude may bounce but still bearish.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ NYMEX July crude may stage a short-lived technical bounce after Tuesday's sharp selloff, and then resume its downtrend.
+ Chartists cited a break below long-term moving averages and a pullback to the April-May rally that exceeded normal Fibonacci retracement levels.

Recovering from Tuesday's sharp selloff, NYMEX crude may consolidate or bounce slightly higher before breaking down to its broad trading range from April between $19 and $20, technical analysts said on Wednesday.

"From the April 4 low of $19.18 to the $22.43 high on May 16, we've corrected over 62 percent of that decline, breaking a number of moving averages that have worked well in this market," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM in New York.
"Over the near term we may have a possible corrective rally but we'll look for limited upside," he said. "Daily studies are still firmly bearish and not as oversold as they could be."
Siller's downside targets were $19.80, $19.50 and then $19.18, with resistance at $20.55 and $20.75, which were previous support areas.

"We're still looking at the much larger trend being up and the short term trend, which had been up from the swing low around $19.18, of course is now down," said Claudia LaCovey, technical analyst at Analytics Research Corp in Bethesda, Maryland.
"Today we're looking to play from the short side with our first significant resistance around $20.65, which had held up the market last week, and above that at $21.19," she added.
The break of $20.61 on Tuesday turned the immediate trend lower, LaClovey said, and the next technical floor is $20.18.
July gasoline was also on the defensive, having failed to exceed its previous swing highs from March 19 when it rallied in mid-May, she said. Her next support area was 59.50-59.70 cents a gallon.
